user_questions.question: All 92 existing reviews have a blank Status__c (none are Submitted or Published). Which rule should the average use? (a) Count only Status = Published, and backfill the 92 legacy reviews to Published as a data step; (b) Count only Published and leave legacy reviews out (all storefront averages go blank until reviews are published); (c) Exclude only Submitted, so blank-status legacy reviews and Published reviews count and no backfill is needed. Recommendation: (a). Also: which average — only Storefront__c.Average_Review_Score__c, or also the averageRating computed by AgentSummarizeReviewsActions (recommended: both)? And should the existing Total_Score__c / Total_Reviews__c roll-ups be filtered in place (changes 'Total Reviews' on the layout and in Get_Partner_Quality_Watchlist) or kept with new filtered roll-ups (recommended: new roll-ups)?
user_questions.simulated_answer: Average should exclude Submitted reviews. (For which average and the roll-up approach: No preference; use your recommended default.)

skill_friction: The simulated answer 'exclude Submitted' did not pick among the offered options for blank-status legacy reviews; I interpreted it as option (c) (filter Status != Submitted), which departs from the literal requirement wording 'only count Published'. SKILL.md has no guidance for an answer that restates the requirement rather than choosing an option.
The askcoworker call kind list has no way to record that the single scope message bundled three questions; recorded as one user_question.

AskCoworker repeatedly cited 'prior session' facts (DataStreams, auto-publish flow) and asserted wrong platform behavior (formula returns blank without FLS on referenced fields; current formula returns 0; bulk roll-up deferral) with blocking labels; the skill's rule to fix without follow-ups worked but these made R/T open-decision lists mostly unusable.
RUNNER seq numbering: org queries were batched in multi-command Bash calls, so one seq covers several queries; the protocol does not say whether each sf command needs its own seq.
